title: Solid-State Battery Architecture with Ceramic Electrolyte Interface
abstract: A novel solid-state battery design featuring a ceramic-polymer composite electrolyte that achieves ionic conductivity comparable to liquid electrolytes while eliminating flammability risks. The architecture incorporates a gradient interface layer between the ceramic electrolyte and electrode materials to reduce interfacial resistance and enable operation across a wide temperature range.

claims.text: A solid-state electrochemical cell comprising: a lithium metal anode; a ceramic-polymer composite electrolyte layer having an ionic conductivity of at least 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees Celsius; a gradient interface layer disposed between the electrolyte and cathode having a composition that transitions continuously from electrolyte composition to cathode composition; and a layered oxide cathode material with a nickel content of at least 80 percent.

The electrochemical cell of claim 1, wherein the ceramic-polymer composite electrolyte comprises garnet-type lithium lanthanum zirconium oxide particles having an average diameter of 100 to 500 nanometers dispersed in a polyethylene oxide matrix at a weight ratio of 60:40 to 80:20.

A method of manufacturing a solid-state battery comprising: preparing ceramic electrolyte particles through a sol-gel synthesis process; blending the ceramic particles with polymer binder at elevated temperature; casting the composite into films of 20 to 100 micrometers thickness; laminating the films with electrode materials under pressure of 10 to 50 MPa; and sintering the assembled cell at a temperature between 600 and 800 degrees Celsius in an inert atmosphere.

detailed_description: Solid-state batteries represent the next generation of energy storage technology, offering substantially improved safety and energy density compared to conventional lithium-ion batteries with liquid electrolytes. The primary challenge in solid-state battery development is achieving sufficiently high ionic conductivity in the solid electrolyte while maintaining mechanical integrity and chemical stability at electrode interfaces. The present invention addresses these challenges through a carefully engineered ceramic-polymer composite that leverages the high conductivity of garnet-type ceramics while the polymer matrix provides mechanical flexibility and conformability to electrode surfaces. The gradient interface layer eliminates the abrupt compositional transition that causes high interfacial resistance in conventional solid-state designs.
